match.reason: No bank point teaches break-even analysis: solving equations with graphs and linear functions are related but broader ideas without the cost, revenue and profit context.

draft.title: Break-even analysis
card: A business has a cost line and a revenue line. Cost = fixed cost + cost per item × number of items. Revenue = price per item × number of items.
The break-even point is where the two lines meet. Cost equals revenue there, so the profit is zero.
Past the break-even point, revenue is above cost and the business makes a profit. Before it, cost is above revenue and the business makes a loss. Profit = revenue − cost.
Example: Ravi sells scarves. Fixed cost is $300 and each scarf costs $10 to make and sells for $25. Set 300 + 10n = 25n. Then 300 = 15n, so n = 20. He breaks even at 20 scarves.
draft.remember: Break even where cost = revenue. Profit = revenue − cost.

a.q: At 50 items, a business has revenue of $900 and cost of $900. What does this show?
opts: It makes a profit at 50 items
It makes a loss at 50 items
a.why: Revenue equals cost, so profit is $0 and 50 items is the break-even point. A profit would need revenue above cost. Fixed cost cannot be found from these two figures alone.

b.q: Mia sells candles. Fixed cost is $400, each candle costs $6 to make and sells for $14. How many candles must she sell to break even?
b.why: Set 400 + 6n = 14n, so 400 = 8n and n = 50. Check: cost is 400 + 300 = $700 and revenue is 14 × 50 = $700. Dividing by the price of $14 gives 29, which ignores that each candle also costs $6 to make.
b.clue: Each candle adds to revenue by the price, minus the cost to make it.

problems.detail: The clue says each candle 'adds to revenue by the price, minus the cost to make it'. Each candle adds $14 to revenue. It is profit that each candle raises by the price minus the making cost ($8). A student could take the clue as a wrong definition of revenue.

check.summary: Both questions and their answers are correct (break-even at 50 items; 400 ÷ 8 = 50 candles). The only problem is that question b's clue wrongly says each candle adds price minus cost to revenue, when it adds that amount to profit.
